short.q: Describe how employment structure changes as a country develops.
short.model: Employment moves from mostly primary in low-income countries, to secondary as factories grow, then to tertiary and quaternary in high-income countries.

short.q: Explain two reasons why manufacturing jobs have fallen in a developed country.
short.model: Globalisation moved factories to cheaper-labour countries, and mechanisation replaced workers with robots, so fewer people are needed.

short.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of informal employment.
short.model: It provides income where formal jobs are scarce; but pay is low and unreliable with no job security or tax paid.

short.q: Explain one positive and one negative impact of a shift to secondary employment in an emerging country.
short.model: Positive: higher wages and a positive multiplier as workers spend money. Negative: pollution and overcrowding in cities as migrants arrive.

short.q: Compare the views of Malthus and Boserup on population and resources.
short.model: Malthus thought food supply cannot keep up with population, leading to famine; Boserup thought population growth drives innovation so food supply rises.
